_: Every test.skip() in e2e/race is registered here, and scripts/check-race-skips.mjs refuses one that is not. A `title` is the case's full name — every describe title down to the leaf, joined with ' > ' — because a leaf title alone can name two different cases. That is not unique either, so the checker refuses a name matching more than one collected case rather than counting it once. An entry either names the test that keeps its reason true (`guardedBy` — that test failing or disappearing is how the reason's expiry surfaces), or states in `unguarded` that nothing does and what observation would settle it. The prose reason stays in the comment beside the skip; what is here is the link a reader cannot make by eye.

collect._: A FLOOR on what each project collects, per file — minCases for --project=race, minCasesWebkit for --project=race-webkit, which race.yml runs as its own job and which no other assertion here reaches (a case leaves it by losing its @webkit tag, which the race floor cannot see). Everything else in this ledger asks about the cases Playwright did collect, so a case that stops being collected is invisible to it: short of a total collection failure, deleting a case or a whole file leaves every other assertion satisfied and check:skips green. A minimum rather than an exact count — adding cases must not be a chore, and what this guards against is loss. check-race-skips.mjs prints every file that has grown past its floor, in this shape, so raising one deliberately is a copy-paste.
collect._shardWeights: How many cases each `--shard=k/N` takes, handed to Playwright as PWTEST_SHARD_WEIGHTS — race.yml reads this array, and its LENGTH is N, so the matrix and this agree or Playwright refuses the run outright. Playwright's own split is a contiguous slice of the collected order sized by case COUNT, and the six expensive t2*-shape-change files sit beside each other in path order, so the equal counts it produces are not equal times. Same order, cut by measured duration instead. Re-derive with `node scripts/race-shard-weights.mjs <run id>` whenever the corpus moves; the reading behind the current array, and what it buys, are in docs/{en,ja}/live-race-harness.md. check-race-skips.mjs re-runs the collection under these weights and fails when a count no longer matches, which is what a corpus that changed SIZE produces, and what a Playwright that stopped honouring an environment variable its own types never documented produces. A one-for-one swap leaves every count alone: nothing reports that the durations behind the array have moved, only a re-derivation shows it.

skips.title: T8 stress > a thirty-minute session leaks no subscription, timer or plan
skips.unguarded: Recorded in docs/{en,ja}/live-race-harness.md as a known gap: the assertions need module-scope state that none of the harness's four surfaces carries. Costed on 2026-08-13 rather than left as a wish. Undo depth is ALREADY on the VITE_TRACE probe (trace-probe.ts's depth()); the MIDI bound-cache size is a Map on MidiControl and would be one hook; a subscription count is one counter in the control layer; armed timers would need the probe to wrap setTimeout/setInterval at boot, which is contained because the probe only exists in a trace build. The fifth — how many Plan objects a writer can still reach — needs a forced collection, and CDP's HeapProfiler.collectGarbage provides one without any launch flag (a Playwright CDP session is available to any Chromium project; the race project is Chromium), so a WeakRef count or Runtime.queryObjects is reachable in the Chromium-only race project. ⚠️ An earlier version of this entry called that impossible; it was not measured and was wrong. So all five readings are within reach and this is work rather than a dead end — what it is not is small: five readings, a probe surface for four of them, and a duration to choose.
